'''Udo W. Pohl''' is a German [[physicist]] who was Professor at [[Technische Universität Berlin]]. His work on [[Semiconductor|semiconductor physics]] focuses on [[quantum dot]]s.

== Education and career ==

Pohl studied physics at [[RWTH Aachen University]], the [[Free University of Berlin]], and Technische Universität Berlin, where he earned doctoral degree in 1988. His doctoral research involved optical spectroscopy of [[transition metal]] impurities in [[II-VI semiconductor compound|II-VI semiconductors]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pohl |first1=U. W. |last2=Gumlich |first2=H.-E. |title=Optical transitions of different Mn-ion pairs in ZnS |journal=Physical Review B |date=15 July 1989 |volume=40 |issue=2 |pages=1194–1201 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.40.1194 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.40.1194|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1989, he became the group leader of the "Materials Lab" at the Institute of Solid State Physics at Technische Universität Berlin, which was later reorganized as the Center of [[Nanophotonics]] in 2004.<ref>{{cite web |title=Medieninformation Nr. 106 - 2. Juni 2005 |url=https://archiv.pressestelle.tu-berlin.de/pi/2005/pi106.htm |website=TU Berlin}}</ref> His scientific work focuses particularly on the structural and optical properties of [[quantum dot]]s based on [[II-VI semiconductor compound|II-VI]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Türck |first1=V. |last2=Rodt |first2=S. |last3=Stier |first3=O. |last4=Heitz |first4=R. |last5=Engelhardt |first5=R. |last6=Pohl |first6=U. W. |last7=Bimberg |first7=D. |last8=Steingrüber |first8=R. |title=Effect of random field fluctuations on excitonic transitions of individual CdSe quantum dots |journal=Physical Review B |date=15 April 2000 |volume=61 |issue=15 |pages=9944–9947 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.61.9944 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prb/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevB.61.9944|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and III-V<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Seguin |first1=R. |last2=Schliwa |first2=A. |last3=Rodt |first3=S. |last4=Pötschke |first4=K. |last5=Pohl |first5=U. W. |last6=Bimberg |first6=D. |date=15 December 2005 |title=Size-Dependent Fine-Structure Splitting in Self-Organized $\mathrm{InAs}/\mathrm{GaAs}$ Quantum Dots |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.257402 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=95 |issue=25 |article-number=257402 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.257402|arxiv=cond-mat/0610436 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lenz |first1=A. |last2=Timm |first2=R. |last3=Eisele |first3=H. |last4=Hennig |first4=Ch. |last5=Becker |first5=S. W. |last8=Bimberg |first8=D. |last9=Dähne |first9=M. |date=30 December 2002 |title=Reversed truncated cone composition distribution of In0.8Ga0.2As quantum dots overgrown by an In0.1Ga0.9As layer in a GaAs matrix |url=https://pubs.aip.org/aip/apl/article-abstract/81/27/5150/513950/Reversed-truncated-cone-composition-distribution?redirectedFrom=fulltext |journal=Applied Physics Letters |volume=81 |issue=27 |pages=5150–5152 |doi=10.1063/1.1533109 |issn=0003-6951|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[List of semiconductor materials#Compound semiconductors|compound semiconductors]] and their [[epitaxy]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ning |first=Zhijun |last2=Gong |first2=Xiwen |last3=Comin |first3=Riccardo |last4=Walters |first4=Grant |last5=Fan |first5=Fengjia |last6=Voznyy |first6=Oleksandr |last7=Yassitepe |first7=Emre |last8=Buin |first8=Andrei |last9=Hoogland |first9=Sjoerd |last10=Sargent |first10=Edward H. |date=2015-07-16 |title=Quantum-dot-in-perovskite solids |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature14563 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=523 |issue=7560 |pages=324–328 |doi=10.1038/nature14563 |issn=0028-0836|hdl=1807/73386 |hdl-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Using active GaAs-based III-V-quantum dots, novel devices such as [[Laser diode|lasers]] and [[Single-photon source|single-photon emitters]] could be realised at the Institute of Solid State Physics with his involvement.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bimberg |first1=Dieter |last2=Pohl |first2=Udo W. |title=Quantum dots: promises and accomplishments |journal=Materials Today |date=1 September 2011 |volume=14 |issue=9 |pages=388–397 |doi=10.1016/S1369-7021(11)70183-3 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1369702111701833 |issn=1369-7021|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Pohl qualified as an assistant professor in 1999 with work on the epitaxy of semiconductors. In 2009, he was appointed adjunct professor of experimental physics at Technische Universität Berlin.<ref>{{cite web |title=U. W. Pohl |url=https://www.physik.tu-berlin.de/institute/IFFP/matlab/Home_U._W._Pohl.html |website=TU Berlin}}</ref> Pohl is member of the [[German Physical Society]] and since 2017 serves as a co-editor of the Springer Series in Materials Science.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Springer Series in Materials Science |url=https://www.springer.com/series/0856?srsltid=AfmBOopRNN785iv4vdUDcsl4fa1x3nhuhzkwacOBMn_rNxtE6Op-x8zy |access-date=2025-03-02 |website=Springer |language=en}}</ref>

==Publications==
In 2013, Pohl published the textbook ''Epitaxy of Semiconductors''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Pohl |first1=Udo W. |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-32970-8 |title=Epitaxy of Semiconductors |date=2013 |edition=1st |language=en}}</ref> He co-authored the Handbook ''Semiconductor Physics'' with [[Karl Wolfgang Boer|Karl Wolfgang Böer]], which was first published in 2018.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Böer |first=Karl W. |url=https://link.springer.com/referencework/10.1007/978-3-319-69150-3 |title=Semiconductor Physics |last2=Pohl |first2=Udo W. |publisher=Springer International Publishing |year=2018 |edition=1st |location=Cham, Switzerland |language=en}}</ref>
